transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (CTO, Horizon Infra), Liam O'Connor (Platform Engineer), Priya Rao (ML Engineer)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Initial integration discovery focused on SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex patterns, gateway/proxy placement, and rate limits/quotas.
- Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency but evaluating Private (VPC) for compliance.
- Action items: share examples, run benchmark, provide security docs.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain / LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy vs direct API, rate limiting/quotas, observability hooks, VPC/KMS/audit logs

--- Transcript body (timestamps are approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Maya Singh: Yeah hearing you Sam, thanks. We got about 45 minutes, good to go.
[00:10] Arjun Patel: Great. I'll be focused on the integration bits - SDKs, batching, observability, stuff like that.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Cool. For context, Horizon runs a multi-tenant platform for infra automation. We're looking to add assistant features in the console and in alerts, and latency/cost are both critical.
[00:28] Priya Rao: And from ML side, we want to use embedding search for KB retrieval and a chat flow for operators. We'll probably use LangChain or LlamaIndex, whatever integrates best.

[01:05] Samantha Ortiz: Awesome. Quick qualification Qs - what's your expected traffic pattern? Burstiness, tokens per request, etc?
[01:12] Priya Rao: Typical chat request is 200-600 tokens, peak concurrent users might be 120-200 during incidents, with many short embedding ops (64-512 dims) for retrieval. Burstiness is high during incidents.

[02:00] Arjun Patel: That helps. Two quick architecture choices you mentioned: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private/VPC install. What are your compliance needs?
[02:12] Maya Singh: We need SOC 2 and encryption at rest, but also control over egress for some customers - so VPC peering or Private would be preferred long term. For POC though, Hosted would be easier.

[03:00] Samantha Ortiz: Totally. For POC we usually recommend Hosted to iterate quickly, then Dedicated or Private for production if you need isolated capacity or network controls.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: When you say Dedicated, is that isolated GPUs in your cloud, or do we manage nodes?
[03:18] Arjun Patel: Dedicated is reserved pools in our infra - you get capacity guarantees and predictable latency, plus network controls, but the control plane stays with Redwood. Private is the fully customer-managed deployment - can be VPC or on-prem.

[04:05] Priya Rao: For integrations: do you have first-class SDKs that work with LangChain and LlamaIndex? We don't want to hand-roll adapters.
[04:14] Arjun Patel: Yes - SDKs in Python/Node/Go. For LangChain and LlamaIndex we have adapters and examples. Note: in some of our written docs the project name was mis-typed as "LammaIndex" by the doc generator, but the code samples use the right package. We'll send those samples.

[04:50] Samantha Ortiz: We should call out gateway options: you can call Redwood API directly from services, or put a small gateway/proxy inside your VPC for egress control and token routing.
[05:00] Maya Singh: Can that gateway handle per-tenant quotas and per-route rate limits? We need strict quota enforcement for billing.
[05:10] Arjun Patel: Gateway can enforce route-level rate limits and do API key translation. For tenant-level billing you'd typically attach your own tenant-id header and the gateway maps requests to Redwood API keys. We also support per-route quotas at the platform side - rate limiting, concurrency caps, and token quotas.

[06:00] Liam O'Connor: How are rate-limits surfaced? Do you return standard 429s with retry-after?
[06:05] Arjun Patel: Yes, 429 with Retry-After; we also return x-rate-limit headers. You can configure soft vs hard limits. For Dedicated you get more granular QoS controls.

[07:20] Priya Rao: Observability - we need traces, per-request latency, token breakdown, and access to logs for compliance. How do you integrate with our existing telemetry?
[07:30] Arjun Patel: We expose webhooks and an observability API - you can forward traces to your tracing backend, or use our console for per-route dashboards. We have trace hooks that annotate spans with model, seq-length, kv-cache hits. For Private deployment, you get full access to raw logs.

[08:40] Maya Singh: KMS & keys - customers require BYOK for certain data. Do you support customer KMS/HSM?
[08:48] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer managed keys but can do BYOK for enterprise deals. We also provide audit logs and SSO SAML integrations.

[10:00] Liam O'Connor: Regarding caching - you mentioned prefix / KV cache earlier in your docs. Does the SDK expose cache controls? Can we pin cache TTLs per-tenant?
[10:10] Arjun Patel: The runtime performs automatic KV caching for autoregressive generation. For prefix caching and application-level caching we expose hints in the SDK. Per-tenant TTLs are configurable for Dedicated/Private via config. Hosted supports sensible defaults.

[11:45] Priya Rao: For embeddings: do you host embeddings index or do we handle vector DB? We use existing vector DBs - Milvus/Weaviate/FAISS.
[11:55] Arjun Patel: Most customers push embeddings into their own vector DB. We provide batch embedding endpoints and an embeddings SDK that outputs normalized vectors and metadata. We also have small connector examples for Milvus and Weaviate in the repo.

[13:20] Maya Singh: Latency SLOs - what's typical p99 for chat on Dedicated?
[13:28] Samantha Ortiz: Typical p99 depends on model size and batching, but on Dedicated with optimized kernels we see p99 in the low hundreds of ms for efficient models; for longer generation/p65 tokens it will be higher. We'll provide model performance profiles.

[14:40] Liam O'Connor: For burst behavior during incidents - can the Dedicated pool auto-burst to hosted spare capacity? We need reliability during spikes.
[14:50] Arjun Patel: Yes, we have configurable burst to shared capacity with fallback policies. You can set policy to fail-closed or fail-open to a smaller model. We'll document tradeoffs for cost vs latency.

[16:05] Priya Rao: About security review: we have to provide a packet on SSO, SOC2, data residency and egress controls for our customers. Can you provide those?
[16:12] Samantha Ortiz: Yes - we'll send SOC2 cert, SAML SSO docs, network topology for Dedicated/Private, and a template for your security team.

[17:20] Maya Singh: A few specific technical nitty-grittys: how does the SDK handle streaming responses for websockets? We need to stream partial tokens to the UI.
[17:30] Arjun Patel: SDK supports streaming over HTTP/2 and websockets; we have client examples in React and Node that pipe token deltas to the UI. The streaming format is newline-delimited JSON.

[19:00] Samantha Ortiz: Let's get into LangChain patterns - are you doing RAG via LlamaIndex or LangChain agents?
[19:10] Priya Rao: We'll probably use LangChain with an embeddings retriever and a simple chat chain. We want to instrument retrieval quality and be able to repro prompts.

[20:05] Arjun Patel: We recommend storing canonical prompt templates and recording prompt/eval logs; Redwood's console can link regressions to prompt sets. We'll send our eval harness example.

[21:30] Liam O'Connor: About billing and metering - do you meter at token level and provide per-tenant usage?
[21:38] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, token-based metering, plus per-request and per-embedding units. For Dedicated we can expose token breakup per API key and you can map keys to tenants for billing.

[23:00] Priya Rao: One worry: if we put a gateway in front, how much added latency are we looking at?
[23:08] Arjun Patel: Minimal - a well-placed gateway adds ~10-30ms depending on VPC peering. The bigger impact is model selection and batching config. We can run a short benchmark to quantify.

[24:45] Maya Singh: Ok let's define POC success criteria: 1) Latency p95 < 400ms for typical chat; 2) Cost not exceed $X per 10k messages (we'll define X in follow-up); 3) Integration with LangChain and streaming UI working.
[24:58] Samantha Ortiz: Sounds good. We'll work up a benchmark plan that simulates your incident burst and sample prompt set.

[26:10] Liam O'Connor: Any known gotchas with VPC peering? NAT/Egress rules?
[26:18] Arjun Patel: Mostly standard cloud network configs - ensure outbound egress to Redwood endpoints or set up Private Link if needed. We'll share network diagrams for Dedicated/Private.

[28:00] Priya Rao: About function/tool calling - we may want structured outputs to drive automation. Does Redwood support function calling semantics?
[28:08] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, we support function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs with schema enforcement. SDKs can parse and route function calls to your internal services.

[30:10] Maya Singh: For security review, who do we loop in? Is there an enterprise lead?
[30:18] Samantha Ortiz: I'll connect you to our security contact, and Arjun will be the technical SE owner for benchmarks and integration.

[31:30] Arjun Patel: I'll prepare LangChain/LlamaIndex examples showing: 1) direct API calls, 2) gateway proxy pattern, 3) streaming + token accounting. Also sample rate limit configs.

[33:00] Liam O'Connor: If we go Private on-prem later, how much lead time?
[33:08] Arjun Patel: Private on-prem varies but plan for 6-10 weeks including packaging, network approvals, and install. VPC-based Private is faster.

[35:15] Priya Rao: Any docs / links you can share now?
[35:20] Samantha Ortiz: We'll share: SDK repo link, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, gateway sample config, and our SOC2 + SSO docs. Links: https://redwood.ai/sdk (sample), https://redwood.ai/integrations/langchain (examples).

[36:40] Maya Singh: Sounds good. One last question: you mentioned KV cache - can we control cache invalidation for model updates?
[36:48] Arjun Patel: Yes, cache invalidation hooks are exposed in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted you can request clear-by-key and TTLs. We'll add docs.

[38:00] Samantha Ortiz: Ok wrapping up - recap of next steps: Arjun will send code samples and benchmark plan; Sam will send pricing and security docs; Priya will share workload and prompts. Any other items?
[38:12] Priya Rao: Nope that's it.
[38:18] Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
[38:22] Samantha Ortiz: Thanks all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.

[39:00] End call.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "LammaIndex" vs LlamaIndex, Run.ai transcribed as Run dot AI), some punctuation missing.

Referenced artifacts / links during call:
- SDK repo + LangChain examples: https://redwood.ai/integrations/langchain
- Security pack (SOC2/SSO/KMS): will be attached to follow-up email
- Benchmark plan (to be drafted by Arjun)

Recap (short): POC on Hosted to iterate; benchmark on Dedicated with potential Private/VPC for production. Deliverables and owners above.
